# Objective

This knowledgebase article will show you how to setup your SteamVR Trackers to track the position and rotation of StretchSense Studio gloves in space. It is intended for users and VTubers who have Valve Base Station 2.0 units and no VR headset who wish to use SteamVR compatible trackers such as HTC Vive or Tundra Trackers for body tracking in software like [Warudo](https://warudo.app/).

For this guide we will mostly use Tundra Trackers as these provide a good balance between tracking accuracy, physical footprint and battery life compared with other SteamVR compatible trackers. You can optionally mix other trackers for head tracking, but we recommend using the same tracker type for tracking your hand positions.

# Required Materials

## Software

The below software is required for this guide, except those marked as optional:

| **Description** | **Version** |
| --- | --- |
| [Hand Engine](https://stretchsense.com/my-account/) | 3.0.12-PRO, 3.0.11-LITE or higher |
| [Steam Desktop Client](https://store.steampowered.com/about/) | latest |
| [SteamVR](https://store.steampowered.com/app/250820/SteamVR/) | 2.5.5 or higher |

## Hardware

This guide supports the following hardware options:

| **Motion Capture Gloves (choose one)** | **Image** |
| --- | --- |
| [StretchSense Studio Gloves](https://stretchsense.com/mocap-studio/), [Pro Studio for Xsens](https://stretchsense.com/pro-studio-glove-for-xsens-ss/), [Pro Studio](https://stretchsense.com/mocap-pro-studio-2/). | ![image-20240213-002626.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488636) |
| [Pro Fidelity](https://stretchsense.com/mocap-pro-fidelity-glove-2/)(is harder use wrist mounted trackers with this option as they overlap the electronics module on the wrist) | ![image-20240213-003945.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488643) |

| **XR Trackers (choose one or mix and match)** | **Image** |
| --- | --- |
| 3x [Tundra Tracker](https://tundra-labs.com/en-nz/products/tundra-tracker-1?variant=40250107461841) (includes 3x [SteamVR dongles](https://tundra-labs.com/products/steamvr-dongle)).We recommend using a [Super Wireless Dongle – Tundra Labs](https://tundra-labs.com/en-nz/products/dongle-mcdongleface?variant=39477474296017) with Tundra trackers as this only requires a single USB port for all 3 trackers. | ![image-20240213-234339.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488649) |
| 3x [Vive Tracker 3.0](https://www.vive.com/us/accessory/tracker3/) | ![image-20240213-234159.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488655) |
| 3x Vive Tracker 2.0 (you must mount to a wrist strap and not directly on the glove mount due to size) | ![image-20240213-234548.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488661) |

| **Hand Tracker Mounts (choose one)** | **Image** |
| --- | --- |
| 2x StretchSense Studio Optical/Universal Mounts | ![Screenshot 2024-02-15 142757.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488667) |
| [Rebuff Reality Trackstraps Set (Wrists + Belt)](https://rebuffreality.com/products/trackstrap-bundle-for-vive-trackers)(The belt strap can be adjusted to fit around your head by cutting it down to size) | ![image-20240214-195658.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488673) |
| [AMVR 5 Pcs VR Tracker Straps](https://www.amazon.com/Tracker-Adjustable-Tracking-Trackers-Wristband-NO/dp/B07S58VWP6) | ![61AZDbUQvjL._AC_SX466_.jpg](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488679) |

| **Head Tracker Mounts** | **Image** |
| --- | --- |
| [Vive Tracker GoPro Head Mount adapter by morgoth90](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:2949042) + [1x Neewer Stainless Steel D-Ring 1/4" Screw](https://www.amazon.ca/Neewer-Stainless-Mounting-Monopod-Release/dp/B00OOLKD3U/) | ![b8fccffe2851cc9c4c430ac174be94cc_display_large.jpg](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488685)![51QYAWfuDGL._AC_SX425_.jpg](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488691) |
| [GoPro Head Strap + QuickClip](https://www.amazon.ca/GoPro-Strap-QuickClip-Official-Mount/dp/B00F19PYR4) | ![51h2nekX5zL._AC_SX425_.jpg](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488697) |

| **Other Required Hardware** | **Image** |
| --- | --- |
| 3-4x Valve Index Base Station 2.0(A minimum of 3 base stations are required for optimal tracking performance) | ![image-20240213-003347.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488703) |

# 1. Null HMD & Head Tracker Setup

These steps will take you through how to connect and configure two trackers for use with SteamVR.

1. Download and install the [Steam Desktop client](https://store.steampowered.com/about/) and [SteamVR](https://store.steampowered.com/app/250820/SteamVR/).
2. Close the StretchSense App for SteamVR if it is open already.
3. Start SteamVR and connect the Vive tracker and dongle you want to use for head tracking. Make note of the name and serial number that shows up in the SteamVR status window (e.g. `LHR-4B07E0F2`) as you’ll need this later to identify it in the SteamVR System Report.
4. Open `C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\SteamVR\resources\settings\default.vrsettings` in a text editor.
5. Add `"activateMultipleDrivers" : true`, `"forcedDriver": "null"`, to near the top of the `steamvr` section of your `steamvr.vrsettings` config file and save the file. This is needed to force the NULL driver to be on and use the above tracker in place of a real HMD.

```
{
  "steamvr" : {
   "activateMultipleDrivers" : true,
  "forcedDriver": "null",
  "allowAsyncReprojection" : false,
  "allowInterleavedReprojection" : false,
  "allowSupersampleFiltering" : false,
  "enableHomeApp" : false,
  "mirrorViewGeometry" : "1387 675 2272 1270",
  "showMirrorView" : true
 }
}
```

5. Open `C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\SteamVR\drivers\null\resources\settings\default.vrsettings` in a text editor.
6. Secondly Set `"enable" : true` under `driver_null` to enable the null driver and save the file.

```
{
"driver_null" : {
	"enable" : true,
	"serialNumber" : "Null Serial Number", 
	"modelNumber" : "Null Model Number",
	"windowX" : 0,
	"windowY" : 0,
	"windowWidth" : 1920,
	"windowHeight" : 1080,
	"renderWidth" : 1920,
	"renderHeight" : 1060,
	"secondsFromVsyncToPhotons" : 0.01111111,
	"displayFrequency" : 60.0
}
  }
```

7. Start SteamVR, right-click on your head mounted tracker and click **Manage Trackers**(see image below).

![Screenshot 2024-06-11 142748.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488709)

8. In the Steam VR settings select **Manage Trackers** (see below)

![Screenshot 2024-05-23 140815.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488715)

9. Set the **Tracker Role** to **Camera.**Click **Close**and also close SteamVR Settings.

![Screenshot 2024-06-11 142648.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488721)
> NOTE: By default, this assumes the tracker is front facing; if you have it mounted to the back of your head you will need to adjust the offsets for the tracker in your animation software, so the character’s head faces the correct direction.

10. With SteamVR running, go to the SteamVR status window, open the menu and click **Create System Report**.

    ![Screenshot 2025-01-22 150825.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att642514946)
11. In the **Devices** tab, find the SteamVR ID of the tracker that matches the one that will be strapped to your head. E.g `/devices/htc/vive_trackerLHR-xxxxxxxx` for HTC VIVE Trackers or `/devices/lighthouse/LHR-xxxxxxxx` for Tundra Trackers. Take note of the path and ID as this will be used in subsequent steps.
12. Open `C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\SteamVR\resources\settings\default.vrsettings` in a text editor.
13. Add the new section below to `steamvr.vrsettings` called `TrackingOverrides`, replacing `vive_trackerLHR-xxxxxxxx` with the serial number and name of the Tundra tracker you are using for your head, found in step. This will force the head mounted tracker to be used as the HMD tracking point.

    ```
    "TrackingOverrides" : {    
         "/devices/lighthouse/LHR-xxxxxxxx" : "/user/head" 
    }
    ```

> INFO: When using Vive Trackers instead of Tundra Trackers the device path is
> /devices/htc/vive\_trackerLHR-xxxxxxxx
> .

# 2. SteamVR Room Calibration & Setup

1. **NOTE:** For this example, we are using **SteamVR Version 2.5.5** with the **Null HMD driver**, **3x Base Station 2.0s,**and**3x Tundra Trackers** (2x hands and 1x head). This guide does not require VR controllers to be connected.
2. Start SteamVR
3. Turn on your base stations, conduct the Room Setup and choose **Standing Only** when prompted.

   ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 142245.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488727)![Screenshot 2024-06-11 142054.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488733)
4. Put the strap with the head mounted tracker attached on your head and ensure the tracker is turned on and paired with the SteamVR dongle connected to your PC, then click **NEXT**.

   ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 144246.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488739)
5. Stand in the position you will be using during your animation. If it’s at your desk, stand up in front of the desk near where you usually sit. Otherwise stand in the middle of your capture space. If you don’t have a VR controller connected, you can use a wireless mouse and click **CALIBRATE CENTER**. Click **NEXT** when done.

   ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 144306.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488745)
6. On the next screen, manually enter your height when prompted and click **Calibrate Floor**. Click **NEXT** when done.

   ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 144418.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488751)
7. With SteamVR running, go to the SteamVR settings menu and toggle **Show Advanced Settings**. Adjust the following setting: **Video → Pause VR when headset is idle** and set it to **Off**. This will allow SteamVR to send tracker data to your animation application and is necessary when using the **Null headset** driver in SteamVR.

   ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 142444.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488757)![Screenshot 2024-06-11 142949.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488763)![Screenshot 2024-05-23 140040.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488769)
8. In the Dashboard tab of the SteamVR settings, set **VR Dashboard on System Button** to **Off**. This will prevent the dashboard from appearing which can block the output of Tundra Tracker data to animation software, Unreal Engine and Unity.

   ![image-20240611-025906.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488775)

# 3. Tundra Tracker Setup for Hand Tracking

1. Mount each Tundra Tracker to the track straps or directly to your gloves as per the [Correcting Hand Rig Offsets for Tundra Trackers](https://stretchsense.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/346980355/Unity+VR+Vive+Tracker+Guide#Correcting-Hand-Rig-Offsets-for-Vive-Trackers) section of this guide. Ensure that the trackers are fastened tightly.
2. Connect your Tundra Trackers as per the device manufacturers instructions. Once the trackers are paired right-click on one of the trackers and click **Manage Trackers**(see image below).

   ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 142748.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488709)
3. In the Steam VR settings select **Manage Trackers** (see below)

   ![Screenshot 2024-05-23 140815.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488715)
4. For the trackers you have connected leave the **Tracker Role** set to **Left Elbow or Right Elbow** depending on which hand you have attached the trackers to**.**Click **Close**and also close SteamVR Settings.

   ![Screenshot 2024-06-04 112013.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488803)
5. Leave SteamVR running in the background and begin to setup your SteamVR compatible software that supports SteamVR trackers, like Virtual Motion Capture (VMC).

# Correcting Hand Rig Offsets for Tundra Trackers

Different Tundra Tracker mounting positions need adjusted offsets for the **left** and **right** hands in your animation software. For these examples we will show how to account of this in Virtual Motion Capture, assuming that you follow the mounting orientations as pictured.

## StretchSense Studio Optical / Universal Mount Offset Correction

StretchSense provides an optional first-party mount to attach smaller trackers directly to [StretchSense Studio Gloves](https://stretchsense.com/mocap-studio/). This provides the best balance of tracking accuracy for the hand orientation as it accounts for wrist bending like with the Palm Ring straps but doesn’t put extra pressure on your hand.

> TIP: When
> ordering Studio Gloves from the StretchSense website
> select Optical/Universal Mounts from the drop-down menu.

- Mount the trackers using a 1/4 inch photography screw with the Tundra base plate attached to the tracker.
- Orient the trackers so the power LED is facing away diagonally from your wrist.
- The tracker should be aligned so the base is square with the mount.
- The USB charging port should be facing towards your wrist diagonally. This allows charging both the glove and Tundra trackers with the charge cables facing the same direction.
- The orientation of both trackers on the mounts should be mirrored.

![Image (28).jpeg](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488809)![Image (27).jpeg](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488815)

- You should only need minor adjustments to the position offsets to account for the raised mount on the glove. The ones suggested below are close to where the tracker will sit on a Size 2 Studio Glove.
- In most cases you will just need to set the rotation of **left-** and **right-hand** offsets to correct the hand orientation in your animation software.

![Screenshot 2024-06-04 145516.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488821)![Screenshot 2024-06-04 145536.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488827)
> INFO: The optical / universal mount for Studio Gloves causes some slight wobbling of the trackers during use. If your animation software supports smoothing or filtering of motion capture data sources, enable list for best performance.

> NOTE: For animations where the user must move their hands quickly, we recommend using palm ring straps to mount Tundra Trackers instead of the optical / universal mount.

## Wrist Strap Hand Offset Correction

See the Unity VR Vive Tracker guides section for [Wrist Strap Hand Offset Correction](https://stretchsense.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/346980355/Unity+VR+Vive+Tracker+Guide#Wrist-Strap-Hand-Offset-Correction) on how to mount Tundra trackers to this kind of strap. Ideally do this so the wrist joint is oriented in your animation software in such a way so minimal rotation offset adjustment is required.

## Palm Ring Straps Hand Offset Correction

See the Unity VR Vive Tracker guides section for [Palm Ring Straps](https://stretchsense.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/346980355/Unity+VR+Vive+Tracker+Guide#Palm-Ring-Straps-Hand-Offset-Correction) on how to mount Tundra trackers to this kind of strap. You will need to adjust the rotation of the tracker so both trackers are mirrored. Ideally do this so the wrist and/or palm joint is oriented in your animation software in such a way so minimal rotation offset adjustment is required.

## Head Tracker Mounting

Assemble the 3D printed mount and attach it to a GoPro head strap as pictured. If using a Vive Tracker as the head mount, make sure the charge port and LED is facing upwards. You will need to adjust the orientation if using a Tundra Tracker. When performing a calibration in software like Virtual Motion Capture, it will automatically compensate for the orientation of the tracker. You may need to adjust the Z offset of the tracker in your animation software with this mount as it is not flush with your forehead.

![Image (36).jpeg](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488833)![Image (32).jpeg](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488839)

# Connecting to Animation Software

There are a few ways to get StretchSense glove data out into your animations to combine finger animations with the position and rotation of the Tundra Trackers.

## Virtual Motion Capture

1. Open Hand Engine, connect and calibrate your gloves.
2. Go to **Edit ->Settings** and toggle **VMC Streaming** to **On**.

   ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 152505.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488845)
3. Open Virtual Motion Capture.
4. Click **Open VRM** and select your VRM model file or connect your VRoid Hub account and download your chosen VRM model.

   ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 152210.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488851)
5. Click the **Setting** button and check the box next to the first entry under **VMC Protocol receiver**. Make sure the **Port** is set to the port used for VMC streaming in Hand Engine (the default is `39540`).

   ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 152003.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488857)
6. Select the first entry in the VMC Protocol receiver list and click the **Edit** button.
7. Check the boxes next to **Left Finger** and **Right Finger**, then click **Close**.

   ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 160942.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488863)
8. Back on the **Settings** menu, click the **Open tracker assignment settings** button and set your **Head**, **Left-hand** and **Right-hand** assigned trackers from the list. If you need to, go back to the SteamVR tracker settings and note which tracker is which, before returning for this screen:

   ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 152026.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488869)
9. Optionally, adjust the left-hand and right-hand tracker offsets to compensate for the position of the tracker based on your chosen tracker mounting option. You can test the effectiveness of any offset adjustments by pushing your hands together in a “pray” gesture and see if both palms contact on your character.
10. Click **Close** when done.
11. Back on the VMC control panel, click **Calibration**:

    ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 152210.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488851)
12. Under **Standard mode** select **I-pose**. On the VMC viewport will have spheres representing the **head**, **left-hand** and **right-hand** trackers line up with the correct position on your VRM character’s body:

    ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 152153.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488886)
13. Click the **Calibration** button then move your body while looking at the resulting screen, put your hands down by your sides with the palms facing your legs. Make the spheres representing the trackers line up with the correct position on your VRM character’s body. Hold the position until the countdown completes and after 5 seconds the calibration will be applied to the character.
14. Once the calibration finishes, a confirmation message will appear:

    ![Screenshot 2024-06-11 160526.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488892)
15. Check your character’s tracking performance and if needed, go back to the **Settings** menu and click **Hand Rotate Fix** and **Calibration Setting** buttons to adjust the character height and hand rotation to compensate for the tracker orientation.

![Screenshot 2024-06-11 151403.png](atlas-asset://confluence-attachment-att574488898)

## Warduo

1. Follow the StretchSense integration guide for [Warudo](https://youtu.be/lbKq81QT5nQ?si=6Qqps8vEAKLlqsbQ) to get setup to receive finger animation data from Hand Engine.
2. For hand position tracking, you will also need to download the paid version of Virtual Motion Capture (available on the VMC developer’s [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/sh_akira) or [pixivFANBOX](https://akira.fanbox.cc/)) in order to output the tracking to Warudo.
3. Follow the [Warudo VMC integration guide](https://docs.warudo.app/docs/mocap/vmc) to setup for hand position and rotation tracking.

<https://youtu.be/lbKq81QT5nQ?si=6Qqps8vEAKLlqsbQ>
